result:
No. Redis adds an operational dependency to solve problems you don't have.

Every reason to add Redis fails against your constraints:

- Caching: a single Elixir process already has ETS, which is in-memory, in-process, and faster than a network round-trip.
- Coordination and locking: you have one writer and one host, so there is nothing to coordinate.
- Persistence: SQLite already owns durable state, and your boot-restore flow works. Adding a second stateful store creates a consistency question (which one is authoritative on restart?) that doesn't exist today.
- Pub/sub: Phoenix PubSub and Registry cover this inside the BEAM without infrastructure.

The cost is real: another service to deploy, monitor, back up, and secure, plus a new failure mode where Redis being down degrades a service that currently depends only on the local disk.

Revisit if one of these changes: multiple nodes needing shared ephemeral state, rate limiting or sessions across hosts, or a queue whose consumers are separate services. Until then, ETS plus SQLite is the right architecture.
